title: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
summary: Light sometimes behaves as a wave (interference, diffraction) and sometimes as a particle (photon). The photoelectric effect showed that light comes in energy packets: each photon has energy E = hν.
To eject an electron from a metal you need at least the work function φ. One photon gives its energy to one electron; what is left becomes the electron's maximum KE — K_max = hν − φ (Einstein).
If the frequency is below the threshold ν₀, no electron comes out however bright the light is. Increasing intensity increases only the NUMBER of electrons (the current), not their maximum KE.
The reverse is also true: moving particles (electrons, protons) behave like waves — de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p. Electron diffraction (Davisson–Germer) proved it.

formulas.name: Photon energy
formulas.note: The 1240 shortcut works only with λ in nm.

formulas.name: Photon momentum
formulas.note: A photon has zero rest mass but still has momentum.

formulas.name: Number of photons
formulas.when: Photons per second from a source of power P.

formulas.name: Work function and threshold
formulas.when: Threshold frequency / wavelength of a metal.
formulas.mistake: Emission only if ν > ν₀ (or λ < λ₀).

formulas.name: Einstein's photoelectric equation
formulas.formula: K_max = ½mv²_max = hν − φ = h(ν − ν₀)
formulas.note: This is the MAXIMUM KE; many electrons come out with less.

formulas.name: Stopping potential
formulas.when: Reverse voltage that makes the photocurrent zero.
formulas.mistake: V₀ does not depend on intensity, only on ν and the metal.

formulas.name: V₀ vs ν graph
formulas.formula: Straight line: slope = h/e (same for every metal),  x-intercept = ν₀,  y-intercept = −φ/e

formulas.name: Radiation force on a surface
formulas.formula: Fully absorbing: F = P/c.   Fully reflecting (normal incidence): F = 2P/c

formulas.name: Charged particle through potential V
formulas.formula: λ = h/√(2mqV);   electron: λ ≈ 1.227/√V nm = 12.27/√V Å

formulas.name: Thermal particles
formulas.when: Gas molecules / thermal neutrons at temperature T.

formulas.name: Ratios to remember
formulas.formula: Same K: λ ∝ 1/√m.   Same V: λ ∝ 1/√(mq).   Same speed: λ ∝ 1/m.   Same p: same λ

examples.title: Energy of a green photon
examples.problem: Energy of a photon of λ = 500 nm in eV?

examples.title: Photoelectric: K_max and V₀
examples.problem: Light of λ = 400 nm falls on a metal with φ = 2.0 eV. K_max and stopping potential?

examples.title: Threshold wavelength
examples.problem: A metal has φ = 2.48 eV. Threshold wavelength?
examples.solution: λ₀ = 1240/φ = 1240/2.48 = 500 nm. Longer wavelengths (red light) cause no emission.

examples.title: How many photons per second?
examples.problem: A 2 W source emits λ = 662 nm. Photons per second? (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s)

examples.title: h and ν₀ from the graph
examples.problem: For a metal, ν = 6.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz gives V₀ = 0.50 V and ν = 8.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz gives V₀ = 1.33 V. Find h and the threshold frequency.

examples.title: de Broglie wavelength of an electron
examples.problem: An electron is accelerated from rest through 100 V. λ?
examples.solution: λ = 1.227/√100 nm = 0.123 nm — similar to X-rays, which is why crystals diffract electrons.

examples.title: Proton vs alpha, same V
examples.problem: A proton and an alpha particle are accelerated through the same V. λ_p : λ_α?

examples.title: Wavelength of a cricket ball
examples.problem: A 0.1 kg ball moves at 10 m/s. de Broglie λ?
examples.solution: λ = h/(mv) = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ / 1 = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ m — so tiny that no slit or atom can diffract it. That is why wave nature is not seen for large objects.

examples.title: Push of light
examples.problem: 3 W of light falls normally on a perfectly reflecting mirror. Force?
examples.solution: F = 2P/c = 2 × 3 / 3 × 10⁸ = 2.0 × 10⁻⁸ N. On an absorbing surface it would be half.

topics.title: Hertz and Lenard's observations
topics.explain: Hertz noticed that sparks jump more easily across a spark gap when UV light falls on it. Lenard showed that UV light ejects negatively charged particles (electrons) from a metal plate and a current flows in the circuit — the photoelectric effect.

topics.title: Four laws of the photoelectric effect
topics.explain: (1) Each metal has a threshold frequency ν₀; below it no emission occurs, whatever the intensity. (2) Emission is instantaneous (~10⁻⁹ s), with no delay. (3) K_max increases linearly with frequency and is independent of intensity. (4) The photocurrent (saturation current) is proportional to intensity.

topics.title: Why the wave theory failed
topics.explain: Wave theory predicted that brighter light would give more energy and that even low-frequency light would eject electrons after some delay. It could explain neither the threshold nor instantaneous emission. The photon model (one photon → one electron) explained all of these.

topics.title: Properties of photons
topics.explain: Energy hν, momentum h/λ, speed c, zero rest mass, zero charge. Higher intensity means more photons, each with the same energy. In photon–electron collisions both energy and momentum are conserved.

topics.title: Graphs (current vs voltage)
topics.explain: Same frequency, different intensity: different saturation current, SAME stopping potential. Same intensity, different frequency: higher ν gives a larger (more negative) stopping potential, saturation current roughly the same. K_max vs ν: straight line, slope h, x-intercept ν₀.

topics.title: de Broglie hypothesis
topics.explain: If light (a wave) can behave like particles, particles can behave like waves: λ = h/p. Large objects have extremely small λ, so wave nature shows up only for light particles like electrons.

topics.title: Davisson–Germer experiment
topics.explain: 54 V electrons were fired at a nickel crystal; a strong peak appeared at 50° — electron diffraction. The measured λ ≈ 0.165 nm matched the de Broglie value of 0.167 nm. First proof of matter waves. Experimental details are no longer in the syllabus — remember the conclusion.

topics.title: Wave–particle duality
topics.explain: Both radiation and matter are dual. A single experiment shows only one face: interference and diffraction show the wave; photoelectric and Compton effects show the particle.

ratta: K_max = hν − φ = eV₀.  Intensity → current; frequency → K_max.
